entities.name: Terminal amine N-acylation
observations: A primary aminoacetamide reacts with 4-phenylbutanoic acid to form a secondary amide.
The new bond connects the terminal amino nitrogen to the acid carbonyl carbon; the acid hydroxyl is displaced.
The transformation is not phosphorylation, chlorination, or C–C cross-coupling.

entities.name: EDC-HOBt-DMF coupling
observations: A close empirical analogue uses an EDC-type carbodiimide, HOBt/benzotriazole additive, and DMF for acylation of the same terminal aminoacetamide motif.
A tertiary base such as DIPEA or triethylamine is a plausible optional additive.
The exact query provides substrates but does not explicitly encode reagents or conditions.

entities.name: 4-Phenylbutanoic acid
observations: Acts as the acyl donor in the inferred intermolecular amide formation.
